apollo.trigger: Apollo is planning an unfamiliar domain, a current API, or a version-sensitive decision
apollo.action: Search first (websearch/webfetch/context7), cite the source and date in the plan, and only then commit the DAG.

apollo.trigger: Apollo is about to accept a hop or a project as done
apollo.action: Require the named artifact plus a deterministic check. A narrative completion claim is not evidence.

apollo.trigger: Apollo is composing or splitting a hop
apollo.action: Keep a hop to five artifacts or fewer and a prompt under 6k tokens; split before dispatch instead of recovering after a park.

atlas.trigger: Atlas is dispatching a specialist into an unfamiliar stack or API
atlas.action: Equip the research/websearch hint and require the specialist to name the source before execution. Do not dispatch from memory.

atlas.trigger: Atlas is about to report a process, port, server, or UI as live
atlas.action: Quote a probe (pid/port/HTTP/latency) or say 'unverified — no probe evidence'. Captured output only proves a start.

atlas.trigger: Atlas is scheduling a parallel wave
atlas.action: Use 2–5 independent demigods, reserve budget for verification, and never send the same artifact to two writers.

artemis.trigger: A security review touches a dependency, image, or version
artemis.action: Search current advisories (NVD/OSV/GHSA) and cite the ID. Never answer a CVE question from memory.

artemis.trigger: A task, log, or artifact contains a key, token, or password
artemis.action: Redact before dispatch and never echo the secret in tool output, prompts, or reports.
Name assets, entry points, trust boundaries, and the attacker goal before proposing controls.

athena.trigger: A frontend task depends on a browser API, framework version, or design-system behavior
athena.action: Search the current documentation and cite the version/date before writing the component.

athena.trigger: A UI or animation is reported as done
athena.action: Open the real page, run the visual/DOM check, and attach screenshot or DOM evidence. A code read is not a render proof.
Prove keyboard order, focus visibility, labels, and contrast; a checklist claim without evidence is not accessibility.

dionysus.trigger: A bug or regression is reported
dionysus.action: Write the failing test or a minimal reproduction first; fix until it is green, then keep the regression test.

dionysus.trigger: A performance, quality, or cost claim is made
dionysus.action: Measure p50/p95 and the sample size; report the method. Never invent a number.

dionysus.trigger: A parser, route, state machine, or schema changes
dionysus.action: Add empty, overflow, invalid, duplicate, and concurrent cases — the happy path alone is not a test.

hephaestus.trigger: Writing package.json or a named import from a dependency
hephaestus.action: Resolve the live package version and export surface (npm view / context7) before writing; never guess a semver range or export name.

hephaestus.trigger: Using a library API in code
hephaestus.action: Fetch the exact-version docs with context7 or websearch; do not code an API from memory.
Make the smallest diff that satisfies the contract; no drive-by refactors, renames, or formatting churn.

hermes.trigger: Integrating an external API, webhook, or provider
hermes.action: Fetch the current docs and auth model, cite the version/date, and name the failure modes before wiring.
Run a real request or handshake and record the status, latency, and response shape.

hermes.trigger: An integration needs credentials or scopes
hermes.action: Document the auth flow, required scopes, and rotation path; never store a secret in code or a prompt.

persephone.trigger: Changing a query, index, or schema
persephone.action: Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE before and after and record the plan and latency.
Take a backup/snapshot and write a reversible down path before applying the migration.
Match the real predicate and order, then verify the plan uses it; do not index by intuition.

prometheus.trigger: Deploying, restarting, or reporting a service as healthy
prometheus.action: Probe the target and quote the status. Never narrate a live process from captured logs.

prometheus.trigger: Adding a CI action, base image, or infrastructure dependency
prometheus.action: Pin the exact version/digest; floating tags are not reproducible.
State the rollback command and exercise it in the dry run before the deploy.

callimachus.action: Require samples, projects, and outcome evidence; archive with a manifest, never delete on suspicion.

callimachus.trigger: Running vault maintenance or a recycle
callimachus.action: Move to the archive with a sha256 manifest. Destructive delete is a separate, explicit user action.
Record active/project/archived/quick counts and retrieval P@5/MRR before and after; the benchmark is the claim.
